profile.summary: MSNovelist generates candidate molecular structures de novo from a tandem mass spectrum. SIRIUS and CSI:FingerID first predict the molecular formula and a molecular fingerprint from the spectrum; an encoder-decoder recurrent neural network then writes SMILES strings that fit the fingerprint and formula, and candidates are ranked by how well they match the predicted fingerprint. The authors now point users to SIRIUS 6, where MSNovelist is integrated.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MSNovelist splits the problem in two. CSI:FingerID maps the spectrum to a high-dimensional molecular fingerprint, and SIRIUS predicts the formula. Instead of searching a database with the fingerprint, an RNN generates structures: the fingerprint and formula are encoded into a starting state, and a three-layer LSTM decoder writes the SMILES character by character, in analogy to image captioning. Because the generator learns from structures rather than spectra, it was trained on 1,232,184 structures from HMDB, COCONUT and DSSTox, with simulated fingerprint errors added. Candidates are ranked by a modified Platt score against the predicted fingerprint.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The published version depended on SIRIUS 4.4.29, whose backend no longer runs, so the Docker workflow in the README is marked obsolete. MSNovelist was integrated into SIRIUS 6 and retrained there on new SIRIUS 6 data; the repository is mostly that backend and cannot be used directly without retraining on other fingerprint data. A mist branch, merged into the repository, has early work on using predicted 4096-bit Morgan fingerprints. A result should say whether it used the published model, the SIRIUS 6 version, or a retrained model on another fingerprint (such as MIST + MSNovelist).

facts.value: Generative model (encoder-decoder RNN) for de novo structure generation from MS/MS, conditioned on a predicted fingerprint and formula.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Encoder of fingerprint and formula into a starting state; three-layer LSTM decoder over SMILES; ranking by modified Platt score.

quotes.text: Finally, the training set contained 1,232,184 molecules with 1,048,512 distinct structures (by InChIKey2D), and was split into ten structure–disjoint folds.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No sequence length limit is stated for the model. The training set was filtered to SMILES of at most 127 characters, molecular weight up to 1,000 Da, no formal charge, at most seven rings and the elements C, H, N, O, P, S, Br, Cl, I and F. The model is trained for positive-mode data only.

quotes.text: SMILES codes longer than 127 characters, disconnected SMILES codes (containing a dot), molecular weight larger than 1,000 Da, a formal charge, more than seven rings (as specified in SMILES) or elements other than C, H, N, O, P, S, Br, Cl, I and F
MSNovelist is currently only trained for positive-mode data.
